name: Montirelin
summary: A lab-stable TRH analogue studied in animals for arousal and neuroprotection; essentially no human trial data.
lead: Montirelin (CG-3703, NS-3) is a synthetic analogue of thyrotropin-releasing hormone (TRH) designed to be more stable, longer acting and more centrally active than the natural hormone. Wikipedia traces its origins to patents held by the German company Gruenenthal.

name: Glypromate
summary: The IGF-1-derived tripeptide GPE, a neuroprotection research compound whose analogue trofinetide became an approved Rett syndrome drug.
lead: Glypromate, also called GPE (glycine-proline-glutamate), is a tripeptide that corresponds to the N-terminal fragment of insulin-like growth factor 1 (IGF-1). It is described as having anti-inflammatory and neuroprotective properties in laboratory research.

name: Trofinetide
summary: The first approved Rett syndrome drug, a GPE analogue; a disease treatment with no appearance use documented.
lead: Trofinetide (brand names Daybue, Daybue Stix; Daybu in the EU) is an oral prescription medicine for Rett syndrome, a rare genetic neurodevelopmental disorder, in patients aged two years and older. The US FDA approved it in March 2023, the first drug approved for the condition.

name: Fosgonimeton
summary: Investigational Alzheimer's drug (a dihexa prodrug) with no appearance data.
lead: Fosgonimeton (also ATH-1017 or NDX-1017) is an investigational small molecule developed by Athira Pharma as a prodrug of an active metabolite, dihexa, that enhances signaling of hepatocyte growth factor (HGF) at its MET receptor.  It was studied as a possible treatment for Alzheimer's disease and other dementias rather than for any cosmetic purpose.

name: BNN-20
summary: Preclinical DHEA-derived BDNF mimic studied in Parkinson's mouse models; no human data.
lead: BNN-20 is a synthetic compound described by its developers as a "microneurotrophin": a small molecule, 17-beta-spiro-[5-androsten-17,2'-oxiran]-3beta-ol, derived from the hormone DHEA, that crosses the blood-brain barrier and is reported to lack endocrine side effects.

name: BNN-27
summary: Preclinical NGF-mimicking DHEA analogue; no human data.
lead: BNN-27 (17alpha,20R-epoxypregn-5-ene-3beta,21-diol) is a synthetic neurosteroid analogue of DHEA described as a "microneurotrophin" and an NGF mimetic.  It is reported to be a selective, high-affinity agonist of the TrkA and p75NTR receptors, to cross the blood-brain barrier, and to lack hormonal activity.

name: N-Acetyl Selank Amidate
summary: Acetylated, amidated Selank analog sold as a research chemical; no direct studies.
lead: N-Acetyl Selank Amidate is a synthetic heptapeptide analog of Selank, with the sequence Ac-Thr-Lys-Pro-Arg-Pro-Gly-Pro-NH2, N-terminally acetylated and C-terminally amidated. These changes are described as intended to resist enzymatic breakdown.

name: N-Acetyl Semax Amidate
summary: Acetylated, amidated Semax analog sold as a research chemical; no direct studies.
lead: N-Acetyl Semax Amidate is a synthetic heptapeptide analog of Semax, with the sequence Ac-Met-Glu-His-Phe-Pro-Gly-Pro-NH2, N-terminally acetylated and C-terminally amidated. These changes are described as intended to resist enzymatic breakdown.

name: DNSP-11
summary: An experimental GDNF-derived brain peptide studied only in rats and monkeys, with no human trials and no appearance data.
lead: DNSP-11 (dopamine neuron stimulating peptide-11) is an experimental 11-amino-acid peptide that researchers derived from the pro-region of glial cell line-derived neurotrophic factor (GDNF). It was proposed as a smaller, easier-to-deliver alternative to full-length GDNF, which has shown protective effects on dopamine neurons in animal models and in some Parkinson's disease trials but is difficult to deliver to the brain because of its size .

name: FGL
summary: A lab-made fragment of a neural adhesion protein with rodent memory data and no human trials or appearance evidence.
lead: FGL (the FG loop peptide) is a 15-amino-acid synthetic peptide derived from the second fibronectin type III module of the neural cell adhesion molecule (NCAM). It was reported to activate fibroblast growth factor receptor 1 (FGFR1), mimicking part of the signalling that NCAM performs during cell adhesion .

name: Cenegermin
summary: A prescription nerve growth factor eye drop approved for a rare corneal disease, with no appearance use.
lead: Cenegermin (brand name Oxervate) is a recombinant human nerve growth factor (rhNGF) given as an eye drop, produced in E. coli. It acts on the TrkA and p75NTR receptors and was the first drug approved for neurotrophic keratitis, a rare condition in which damaged corneal nerves lead to persistent epithelial defects . The European Union approved it in 2017 and the United States in 2018 .

name: Mecasermin rinfabate
summary: An IGF-1/IGFBP-3 injectable built for rare growth failure; no data supports height gain in people with normal growth.
lead: Mecasermin rinfabate (brand name Iplex, also called rhIGF-I/rhIGFBP-3) is a complex of recombinant human insulin-like growth factor 1 (IGF-1) bound to recombinant IGF binding protein 3, given by daily subcutaneous injection. It was developed by Insmed to prolong the half-life of IGF-1 and potentially reduce side effects such as hypoglycemia .

name: Axokine
summary: A discontinued CNTF-based injectable for obesity that produced small weight loss in trials and triggered antibodies in most users.
lead: Axokine is a modified recombinant form of human ciliary neurotrophic factor (CNTF) that was developed as an obesity drug by Regeneron Pharmaceuticals. It carries a 15-amino-acid C-terminal truncation and two substitutions, and is reported to be more potent and stable than natural CNTF . It was designed to reduce body weight through a leptin-like mechanism .

name: KTTKS
summary: The collagen-signalling pentapeptide behind Matrixyl, with a modest split-face trial and open questions about skin penetration.
lead: KTTKS is a pentapeptide (lysine-threonine-threonine-lysine-serine) used in anti-wrinkle skin care, usually in its palmitoylated form, palmitoyl pentapeptide-4 (Pal-KTTKS), sold under the trade name Matrixyl. Sederma launched Matrixyl in 2000. It is classed as a matrikine, a messenger peptide that regulates cell activity .

name: Palmitoyl tripeptide-38
summary: A branded cosmetic signal peptide sold as a collagen booster; the evidence is mostly supplier data and multi-ingredient serum studies.
lead: Palmitoyl tripeptide-38 is a synthetic lipopeptide used as a cosmetic anti-wrinkle ingredient. It is sold by Sederma, a subsidiary of Croda, under the trade name Matrixyl Synthe'6, and is described by the supplier as a matrikine mimic, meaning a small signalling fragment intended to prompt the skin to remodel its extracellular matrix .

name: Glycyl-prolyl-hydroxyproline
summary: A collagen-derived tripeptide found in supplements; absorbed in animals, with no human skin trials of the peptide itself.
lead: Glycyl-prolyl-hydroxyproline (Gly-Pro-Hyp) is a tripeptide made of glycine, proline and hydroxyproline, a sequence characteristic of collagen. It is found in collagen hydrolysates, the ingredient in oral collagen supplements and some cosmetic products, and is one of several small peptides studied as a bioactive component of those preparations .

name: AHK-Cu
summary: A copper tripeptide marketed for hair growth, backed so far only by cell-culture research.
lead: AHK-Cu is a copper complex of the tripeptide alanyl-histidyl-lysine, also called copper tripeptide-3. It is marketed in hair-care products and discussed in appearance circles as a hair-growth ingredient, in the way the related GHK-Cu is discussed for skin .

name: LL-37
summary: The body's own antimicrobial skin peptide, now chatted about for acne with no cosmetic trials behind it.
lead: LL-37 is a 37-amino-acid antimicrobial peptide and the only cathelicidin made by humans. It is cleaved from a precursor protein, hCAP18, and is produced by neutrophils and epithelial cells including skin keratinocytes . It is part of the innate immune system and also signals to immune cells .
claims: LL-37 might help clear acne and heal skin

name: Heberprot-P
summary: A Cuban injectable EGF for diabetic foot ulcers; wound-healing evidence is small-scale and nothing exists for cosmetic use.
lead: Heberprot-P is an injectable formulation of recombinant human epidermal growth factor (rhEGF, nepidermin) developed by Cuba's Center for Genetic Engineering and Biotechnology and marketed by Heber Biotec. It is used for advanced diabetic foot ulcers, where it is injected into and around the wound.

name: Palifermin
summary: A prescription keratinocyte growth factor for chemotherapy mouth sores, with no cosmetic evidence.
lead: Palifermin (brand name Kepivance) is a truncated recombinant human keratinocyte growth factor (KGF), a member of the fibroblast growth factor family produced in E. coli. It is approved to reduce the incidence and duration of severe oral mucositis in patients with blood cancers receiving high-dose chemotherapy with stem cell support .

name: Epidermal growth factor (EGF)
summary: A growth-factor protein sold in skincare serums; real biology, one tiny serum trial with no published results.
lead: Epidermal growth factor (EGF) is a small protein of 53 amino acids that stimulates cell growth, differentiation and survival by binding the EGF receptor (EGFR) on cell surfaces . It was the second growth factor to be identified; Stanley Cohen found it while working with Rita Levi-Montalcini, and the two shared the 1986 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine .
claims: Topical EGF serums rejuvenate skin and reduce wrinkles
EGF is a safe skincare ingredient because it is a natural protein

name: CJC/IPA Protocol
summary: The common GH-releasing peptide pairing; popular on forums, untested as a combination, neither part approved.
lead: CJC/IPA refers to the combined use of CJC-1295, a long-acting analogue of growth hormone-releasing hormone (GHRH), and ipamorelin, a selective ghrelin-receptor (growth hormone secretagogue) agonist, both aimed at raising growth hormone (GH) release . Neither is an approved drug.
claims: CJC/IPA causes water retention that changes facial and eye appearance
CJC/IPA might close growth plates early or stunt height

name: Tesa/IPA Protocol
summary: A tesamorelin plus ipamorelin injectable peptide stack for fat loss; each part has some history, the combination has no trials.
lead: The Tesa/IPA protocol is a term used in peptide and body-composition circles for combining two injectable growth-hormone-axis peptides, tesamorelin and ipamorelin. The two are different substances: tesamorelin is a synthetic analogue of growth-hormone-releasing hormone (GHRH), while ipamorelin is a pentapeptide that acts on the ghrelin (growth hormone secretagogue) receptor.
claims: Combining tesamorelin and ipamorelin gives a stronger or complementary growth-hormone release for fat loss

name: GT20029
summary: An experimental topical AR-degrading PROTAC for male pattern hair loss, with a published Phase 2 trial and no approval.
lead: GT20029 is an investigational topical androgen receptor (AR) degrader developed by Kintor Pharmaceutical of China for androgenetic alopecia and acne. It is a PROTAC (proteolysis-targeting chimera), a type of molecule that tags a target protein for destruction by the cell's proteasome rather than merely blocking it.
claims: A topical AR degrader could replace finasteride without systemic side effects

name: Liposomal IGF-1
summary: IGF-1 in liposomes for the scalp; the biology is plausible on paper but evidence is preclinical.
lead: Liposomal IGF-1 refers to insulin-like growth factor 1 packaged in liposomes for topical application to the scalp. IGF-1 is a growth factor made mainly by dermal papilla cells in hair-bearing skin; a 2025 review reports that it stimulates follicle proliferation and vascularization and promotes the growth (anagen) phase through PI3K/Akt and MAPK/ERK signalling.

name: Hedgehog pathway agonist
summary: A discontinued class of topical hair-growth compounds that activated Hedgehog signaling; development reportedly ended over animal toxicity.
lead: Hedgehog pathway agonists are small molecules that switch on the Hedgehog signaling pathway, which guides embryonic development and regulates adult stem cells. The pathway is reported to be required for hair follicles to move from the resting phase into the growth phase, which is why agonists were explored as hair-growth drugs.

name: Adenosine (topical hair)
summary: A cosmetic hair-growth active with plausible lab data on dermal papilla cells; human evidence not established here.
lead: Adenosine is a naturally occurring nucleoside used as a cosmetic active in hair-growth products. Laboratory work reports that it acts on dermal papilla cells, the follicle's signalling center.

name: Procyanidin B2
summary: An apple polyphenol with early lab, mouse and small human data for hair growth, mostly using whole extracts.
lead: Procyanidin B2 is a B-type dimer of the procyanidin subgroup of proanthocyanidins, polyphenols built mainly from catechin and epicatechin units. Apples are a notable dietary source of proanthocyanidins.

name: Garlic gel
summary: A folk garlic preparation for patchy hair loss with one terminated children's trial behind it and a record of skin burns when applied raw.
lead: Garlic gel is a topical preparation made from garlic (Allium sativum) that has been used as a folk or alternative treatment for alopecia areata, an autoimmune condition that causes patchy hair loss. It is discussed mainly in the context of non-prescription approaches to hair regrowth rather than in appearance-optimisation forums specifically.

name: Avobenzone
summary: The main organic UVA filter in US sunscreens: widely used for photoageing protection, unstable in sunlight without stabilisers, absorbed into the bloodstream.
lead: Avobenzone (butyl methoxydibenzoylmethane, trade name Parsol 1789) is an oil-soluble organic compound used as a UVA filter in chemical sunscreens and in moisturisers and cosmetics that carry an SPF claim . It absorbs ultraviolet light across much of the UVA range, with an absorption peak near 357 nm .
